case_studies.title: CreativeInstruct: Scalably Teaching LLMs to Balance Quality, Creativity, and Diversity
case_studies.abstract: While post-training improves the capabilities of large language models (LLMs), it generally lowers their output diversity and creativity, negatively impacting tasks that explicitly require creativity (e.g., story generation) as well as those that require it implicitly, e.g., reinforcement learning (RL). We instead propose CreativeInstruct, a scalable instruction-tuning method that teaches LLMs to balance creative, base-model-like generations with the quality of post-trained models, by learning to inject special [StartCreativity] spans that bias generation toward creativity. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of large language models losing creativity and diversity after post-training, by creating a method called CreativeInstruct that balances quality and creativity, resulting in more diverse and creative outputs. The researchers built a scalable instruction-tuning method that teaches models to inject special spans to bias generation toward creativity. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: PsychoAgent: An Affect-Sensitive Cognitive Architecture for Conflict-Aware Memory in LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: Human-like cognition does not select past experience by topical similarity alone: affective significance and unresolved conflict also shape what becomes accessible. We present PsychoAgent, a cognitive architecture for LLM agents that separates factual and affective memory and integrates both through a conflict-aware executive controller. Affective memories are first filtered by semantic relevance and then re-ranked by salience, preserving topical fit while allowing emotionally important traces to enter the prompt. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of making language models more human-like by considering emotions and past conflicts, the authors built PsychoAgent, a cognitive architecture that separates factual and affective memory, and the result is a more efficient retrieval of relevant memories. This is not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work. The research focuses on improving language models.

case_studies.title: A Domain-Specific Harness for End-to-End Automation of Optimization Research
case_studies.abstract: We present AutoOPT, a domain-specific harness for end-to-end automation of optimization research. AutoOPT organizes the discovery of optimal first-order methods into four stages: numerical design through the BnB-PEP methodology; symbolic discovery of the analytic description and a convergence proof through frontier large language models (LLMs); formal verification in the Lean 4 proof assistant; and human interpretation and write-up. case_studies.summary: Researchers built AutoOPT, a tool that automates the process of finding the best methods for optimization problems, which can help improve the performance of cloud infrastructure. AutoOPT uses a combination of machine learning and formal verification to find the most efficient methods. The result is a faster and more reliable way to optimize complex systems.

case_studies.title: A MARL Centered Reference Architecture for Large Language Model Augmentation in Smart Manufacturing
case_studies.abstract: Modern manufacturing imposes six coupled demands on adaptive control: local decisions with global consequences, partial observability, nonstationarity, reflex speed response with long horizon effects, delayed and diffuse outcomes, and dynamics that resist explicit modeling. Cooperative multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL), posed as a Dec-POMDP under centralized training with decentralized execution, is a particularly natural formalism for these demands. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of adaptive control in smart manufacturing by building a reference architecture that uses cooperative multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL) and large language models (LLMs). The result is a more effective and efficient control system for manufacturing. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Fisher-R1: Training LLM Agents for Reliable Hypothesis Testing
case_studies.abstract: Reliable hypothesis testing is the foundation of many empirical scientific claims. Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used to automate this process, as they can inspect datasets, generate code, and produce analyses end-to-end. However, we show that they frequently make subtle inferential errors that lead to incorrect conclusions despite correctly executed analyses. Existing benchmarks fail to capture this failure mode, as they rarely assess whether a reported p-value is statistically valid given the assumptions underlying the data. case_studies.summary: Researchers found that large language models can make errors in hypothesis testing, leading to incorrect conclusions. They built P-Bench, a benchmark to test the statistical validity of results. This doesn't directly impact cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it relates to the accuracy of large language models in hypothesis testing, not cloud management or operations.

case_studies.title: AgentChaos: Chaos Engineering for Agent Systems via Programmatic Fault Injection
case_studies.abstract: Agent systems rely on LLM APIs for every response, but these APIs can return server errors, truncated responses, or corrupted content that propagates through downstream agents and causes task failure. Evaluating robustness under these faults is crucial for reliable deployment. Existing fault injection methods are offline, require source code modification, or cannot modify specific response fields. A comprehensive evaluation also requires a systematic fault taxonomy because different fault types affect downstream agents differently. We propose AgentChaos, a chaos engineering framework for contr
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating the robustness of agent systems against faults in LLM APIs, by building a chaos engineering framework called AgentChaos that can inject programmatic faults. The result is a comprehensive evaluation framework that can help identify and mitigate potential failures in agent systems. This can help ensure reliable deployment of these systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that relies on LLM APIs, here is what to do: review your current fault tolerance measures, assess the potential impact of LLM API faults on your system, and consider implementing AgentChaos or similar chaos engineering frameworks to evaluate and improve robustness. This flags a risk: if your org uses agent systems with LLM APIs, check your current fault injection methods and evaluate if they are sufficient. Check your system's ability to handle server errors, truncated responses, or corrupted content from LLM APIs immediately.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel AI tooling for robustness evaluation in agent systems using LLM APIs, relevant to AI deployment and security.

case_studies.title: PACE: Primitive-Aware Code Evolution for Automated Algorithm Design
case_studies.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based automated algorithm design typically evolves algorithms as complete, indivisible programs. While this whole-program perspective simplifies the search space, it fundamentally couples the useful local logic to its host program. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of valuable code snippets being lost when overall programs are discarded, by building a system called Primitive-Aware Code Evolution (PACE) that decouples local logic from complete programs. The result is a more efficient way to evolve algorithms using large language models. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: A Picture is Worth a Thousand Tokens: How Vision Language Models Cut AI Energy Costs While Improving Accuracy
case_studies.abstract: LLM inference accounts for over 90% of AI operational energy, scaling directly with input token count---a critical inefficiency for telecom network analytics and numerical time-series data analysis (NTSDA), where raw multivariate KPI windows from 4G/5G cell sites expand into thousands of floating-point tokens. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) eliminate this mismatch by encoding time-series as 2D plots, achieving 3.6-10.4x input token reduction across Llama-3.2-90B, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, and Pixtral-12B architectures. This translates to 1.8-2.5x measured inference energy reduction, saving approximately
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of high energy costs in AI operations by using Vision Language Models to reduce input token count, resulting in a 1.8-2.5x reduction in inference energy. The team built a system that uses 2D plots to represent time-series data, achieving a 3.6-10.4x reduction in input tokens. This leads to significant energy savings for AI operations, particularly in telecom network analytics and numerical time-series data analysis.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI infrastructure, here is what to do: consider implementing Vision Language Models to reduce input token count, check your current token usage and identify areas where 2D plot encoding can be applied, and assess the potential energy savings for your organization.
case_studies.score_reasoning: This paper shows a surprising new approach (VLMs) to AI energy efficiency, but its direct relevance and immediate applicability to IT infrastructure is somewhat limited.

case_studies.title: Beyond Post-Hoc Temperature Scaling: Bilevel Optimization for LLM Calibration
case_studies.abstract: Preference alignment often makes large language models (LLMs) overconfident and poorly calibrated. Traditional post-hoc temperature scaling is inherently domain-dependent: a temperature fitted on one domain does not generalize across domains. This motivates us to modify model parameters during training to improve calibration. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of large language models being overconfident and poorly calibrated by using a bilevel optimization approach to improve calibration. The authors built a new method that modifies model parameters during training to maximize the entropy of predictive distributions. The result is a more accurate and reliable model.

case_studies.title: The Banach lattice Lean library
case_studies.abstract: We present a Lean 4 library for the theory of Banach lattices. Its purpose is to support the systematic formalization of contemporary research in Banach lattices and related areas. As evidence of this, we describe three research-level formalizations built using the library. Writing the library at scale was made possible by the use of LLMs with careful human supervision and planning. Unlike autoformalization, this approach allows for an actual understanding of the code.
